papers.title: Additive Relations and Betti Growth in Goldbach Rings
papers.abstract: The binary Goldbach ring over a field $k$ is the quotient of $R=k[x_p:p\text{ an odd prime}]$ by the relations $x_px_q=x_{p'}x_{q'}$ whenever $p+q=p'+q'$, with $\deg x_p=(p,1)$. We prove that if $g$ is a map from the odd primes to an abelian group and $g(p)+g(q)$ depends only on $p+q$, then $g(p)=g(3)+\frac{p-3}{2}(g(5)-g(3))$ for every odd prime $p$. This settles K\'atai and Phong's conjecture on shifted prime arguments and proves, for odd primes, the affine classification they conjectured for binary sums. The universal group of binary prime relations is free of rank two. We obtain a minimal bigraded free resolution from compatible resolutions of finite truncations and determine the growth of its linear Betti numbers in two regimes. For fixed monomial degree $d\ge3$, as the Goldbach degree $n\to\infty$ through $n\equiv d\pmod2$, we prove $\beta_{d-1,n,d}\sim(d-1)T_d(n)/d!$, where $T_d(n)$ counts ordered representations by $d$ odd primes. Explicit Koszul cycles from common prime shifts span a positive fraction of this strand. For finite supports $\mathcal{A}_m=\{p\le m:p\text{ an odd prime}\}$, fix the homological degree $i\ge1$ and sum over all Goldbach degrees. As $m\to\infty$, the linear-strand totals are asymptotic to $i|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when all binary relations on $\mathcal{A}_m$ are retained, and to $(1-2^{-i})|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when only relations of common weight at most $m$ are retained. These leading estimates are uniform over fields. The interpolation theorem gives eventual depth at most two for the variable truncations; both truncation families have asymptotically maximal projective dimension.

papers.title: Critical schemes, jet syzygies, and twisted periods
papers.abstract: We study nonreduced critical schemes with prescribed support on nilpotent orbit closures and on the Kleinian singularity $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, and show that one specified minimal invariant syzygy among the first jet equations fixes their scheme structure. For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_N$ or $\mathfrak{so}_{2N}$ with Coxeter number $h$ and $p\ge2$ coprime to $h$, the selected polynomial is the coefficient of $s^{p+1}$ in $\det(1-sM)^{p/h}$, with reduced critical locus $\{M^p=0\}$, and the selecting syzygy is equivalent to the twisted period equation of Dubrovin and Feigin-Silantyev. The minimal invariant syzygies of that degree correspond to the lowest nonquadratic twisted periods, which, for $\mathfrak{so}_8$, form the standard representation of triality; in type D the Betti number alone does not determine the scheme. On $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, the selected polynomial is given by a terminating hypergeometric series. Restriction to Slodowy slices commutes with forming critical schemes and their nilradicals. These results determine, uniformly in rank and degree, the rings and nilradical filtrations through which the Schur and Macdonald indices of the corresponding Argyres-Douglas theories are proposed to arise as Hilbert series of arc spaces.

papers.title: A Characterization of Completely Integrally Closed Pr\"{u}fer $v$-Multiplication Domains
papers.abstract: We generalize a result known for Pr\"ufer domains to show that a PVMD $R$ is completely integrally closed if and only if $\text{Inv}^t(R)$ is an archimedean $\ell$-group. It has been conjectured that a PVMD is completely integrally closed if and only if it is an Archimedean domain. It is known that a completely integrally closed PVMD is an Archimedean domain. We provide an example to illustrate that an Archimedean PVMD need not be completely integrally closed.

papers.title: Golod thresholds of ideals and products of ideals in dimension 3
papers.abstract: Let $I$ be a proper ideal in a standard graded polynomial ring $P$ with homogeneous maximal ideal $\m$. We show that there exists $k_0\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\m^kI$ is Golod for all $k\geq k_0$. The smallest such $k_0$ is denoted $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$. We give an explicit formula for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ in the case when $I$ is a monomial complete intersection and bounds for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ for other classes of ideals. We show that under a certain degree condition, the product of a Golod ideal with a maximal homogeneous ideal is Golod. In the last section, we show that in a regular local ring of dimension 3, the product of any two proper ideals is Golod; this solves a question posed by Dao-Stefani \cite[Question 4.5]{dao2022monomial} and VandeBogert \cite[Question 4.11]{vandebogert2022products}.

papers.title: Stability of Hilbert--Samuel functions with linear bounds in homological degree
papers.abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $I$ be generated by a filter regular sequence. Set $A=R/I$, $s=\dim A>0$, and $D= \operatorname{hdeg}(A)$. If $A$ is equicharacteristic, we prove that perturbations of order $(2s+1)D$ preserve the Hilbert--Samuel function in every dimension. In arbitrary characteristic, we obtain the order $[s+(s+1)(k!)^{k-1}]D^k$, where $k$ is the maximum of $1$ and the dimensions of the lower deficiency modules of $\widehat A$. Both bounds depend only on the final quotient. The proof constructs monic annihilating equations for the deficiency modules and uses them to choose a parameter $d$-sequence with an explicit relation to a reduction of the maximal ideal. In the equicharacteristic case, a dimension filtration and characteristic polynomials over regular subrings give equations of degree at most the arithmetic degree, with coefficients in the required powers of the reduction.

papers.title: Face rings and the cohomology of unions of Schubert varieties
papers.abstract: The cohomology ring of a union of Schubert varieties $X_{W}=\bigcup_{w\in W}X_w,$ for $W\subseteq S_n$, in the complete flag variety is well known to be a quotient of the coinvariant ring $R_n$. We determine exactly when the ideal defining this quotient is generated by squarefree monomials, i.e. when it can be identified with the image of a Stanley-Reisner ideal $I_\Delta$ in $R_n$. We prove that a single Schubert variety $X_w$ has this property exactly when $w\in S_n$ avoids a set of seven patterns, and in this case we describe the corresponding doubly-pruned simplicial complex $\Delta$. We then show this is equivalent to $X_w$ being cut out of the complete flag variety by particular inclusion conditions on the pieces of the flag. We prove these complexes are vertex decomposable, and are Cohen-Macaulay precisely when $X_w$ is smooth. We then give a closed formula for the Poincar\'e polynomial of $X_w$. For unions $X_W$, pattern avoidance is necessary but no longer sufficient, and we prove a necessary and sufficient condition we call prunable that describes how the individual complexes associated to each $w\in W$ may be glued in the union. Quotients of $R_n$ by squarefree monomial ideals appear naturally in the Adams-Reiner conjecture on resolutions of Stanley-Reisner rings over certain parameter rings. We prove their conjecture for a family of simplicial complexes that includes the doubly-pruned complexes.

papers.title: Boij-S"oderberg and Harder-Narasimhan polygons of vector bundles on projective space
papers.abstract: Eisenbud and Schreyer proved that the cohomology table of a vector bundle $F$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ is a unique positive combination of supernatural tables along a chain of root sequences. The slopes of the pieces, weighted by their ranks, form a concave polygon $\Psi_F$, the Boij-S\"oderberg polygon, with the same endpoints as the Harder-Narasimhan polygon $P_F$. We prove that $P_F\leq\Psi_F$, in any characteristic, by testing subsheaves against sheaves with pure resolutions on thickened lines; the bound is optimal among bounds depending only on the ray of the table. The chain majorizes every other supernatural decomposition, and $\Psi$ is monotone under cancellations, hence upper semicontinuous in flat families. The comparison extends to coherent sheaves and, by linear projection, to sheaves of positive dimension. On $\mathbb{P}^2$ the defect is a sum of four cohomological terms; we characterize equality and show that the inequality survives the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability. For a smooth projective variety $X$ of dimension $n\geq2$ in characteristic zero, with $H$ ample and base-point-free, the mean normalized squared spread $G(\mathcal{E})$ of the roots in the cohomology table of every vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies $G(\mathcal{E})\geq(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{n-2}/((n+1)H^n)$, a bound independent of $\mathcal{E}$. Since $G(\mathcal{E})=1$ exactly for arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, when this bound exceeds $1$ it is a uniform form of their absence.

papers.title: On the $h$-polynomials of cyclotomic standard graded Cohen-Macaulay rings
papers.abstract: We say that a standard graded algebra is cyclotomic if all roots of its $h$-polynomial lie on the complex unit circle. We study which products of cyclotomic polynomials can occur as $h$-polynomials of standard graded Cohen--Macaulay algebras without being of complete intersection type. For each fixed positive integer $a$, we reduce the nonexistence problem for multiplicities $ap$ over all sufficiently large primes $p$ to finitely many cases. Combining this reduction with explicit constructions, we completely characterize the positive integers $k$ for which such a polynomial of multiplicity $8k$ exists: precisely those satisfying \[k\notin\{1,2,3,6\}\cup\{p:p\ge7\text{ is prime}\}\cup\{3p:p\ge17\text{ is prime}\}.\]

papers.title: Immaculate complexes and Strong Generation by Injectives
papers.abstract: We study the category of bounded complexes of finite sums of indecomposable injectives over a locally Noetherian scheme, which we call the immaculate complexes. We show that regularity and finiteness of dimension can be detected from this category using strong generation. Our methods involve studying when the unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck category is strongly generated by injectives. As applications we prove a conjecture of Hartshorne and recover a result of Keller and Krause. To any specialisation closed subset we associate a semi-orthogonal decomposition of the immaculates and use this to compute additive finitary invariants in terms of the completions of the local rings. The immaculates are equivalent to the perfect derived category of a left coherent preadditive category i.e. a ring with many objects and we compute this category for one-dimensional integral or Gorenstein schemes.

papers.title: Bloch groups of local rings with residue field $\mathbb{F}_2$
papers.abstract: We give a generic presentation of the pre-Bloch group of a local ring with residue field $\mathbb{F}_{2}$. We apply this to the calculation of pre-Bloch groups and Bloch groups of some local rings.

papers.title: Poincar\'e polynomials of nilmanifolds associated with path graphs
papers.abstract: We give explicit and recursive formulas for the Poincar\'e polynomials of Dani--Mainkar nilmanifolds associated with path graphs. We also prove that these polynomials are unimodal, and we calculate a range of Betti numbers asymptotically. As an application, we derive a sharp lower bound for the dimension of the total de Rham cohomology of a Dani--Mainkar nilmanifold.

papers.title: Integer Decomposition Property of Edge Polytopes of Weighted Oriented Graphs
papers.abstract: We classify the lattice polytopes arising from vertex-weighted oriented graphs that have the integer decomposition property (IDP). Allowing vertex weights and edge orientations introduces non-vertex lattice points in the polytope which need to be accounted for when studying the IDP. We can then identify forbidden induced subgraphs in the sense that their presence obstructs the IDP for the supergraph. We establish positive results for several families of graphs under suitable orientation and coprimality conditions, including weighted oriented paths and cycles, and show that any weighted oriented tree with a unique sink has the IDP.

papers.title: Homology with the theme of Matlis
papers.abstract: Matlis proved a lot of homological properties of the fraction field of an integral domain. In this paper, we simplify and extend some of them from 1-dimensional (resp. rank one) cases to the higher dimensional (resp. finite rank) cases. For example, we study the weakly cotorsion property of $\Ext(-,\sim)$, and use it to present splitting criteria. These are equipped with several applications. For instance, we compute the projective dimension of $\widehat{R}$ and present some non-noetherian versions of Grothendieck's localization problem. We construct a new class of co-Hopfian modules and extend Matlis' decomposability problem to higher ranks. In particular, this paper deals with the basic properties of Matlis' quadratic $(Q,Q/R, \widehat{R},\overset{\sim}R).$

papers.title: Applications of reduced and coreduced modules III: Derived torsion and completion over polynomial extensions
papers.abstract: We study when degree-zero identities for reduced and coreduced modules extend to ambient derived torsion and completion. For a non-idempotent ideal $I$ in an explicit polynomial ring, we construct a module $M$ that is simultaneously $I$-reduced and $I$-coreduced and satisfies $\Gamma_I(M)=\Lambda_I(M)=0$ but $H_I^2(M)\ne0$. The module is a union of finite reduced and coreduced submodules whose positive derived torsion vanishes. The supporting ideal has unrestricted torsion dimension two, whereas the dimension on each bounded-nilpotence quotient category is one. The calculations use compatible cone resolutions for $R=S[t]$ and $I=JS[t]+(t)$, where $J^2=J$. These give paired Ext--Tor formulas for coefficients annihilated by a fixed power of $t$. For arbitrary coefficients, an explicit mapping-fiber model realizes the standard derived-composition comparison sequence and identifies the obstruction to extending the bounded formula. Coordinate calculations for countably idempotent-generated ideals supply the computational foundation, and a valuation-domain example gives nonzero first derived completion on a cyclic reduced and coreduced coefficient.

papers.title: Fedder-type criterion for quasi-$F^e$-splitting and quasi-$F$-regularity
papers.abstract: We study quasi-$F^e$-split and quasi-$F$-regular singularities, which generalize Yobuko's quasi-$F$-splitting. We establish Fedder type criteria that characterize these properties for hypersurfaces. These criteria offer explicit tools for computation and verification. As an application, we construct a counterexample to the inversion of adjunction for quasi-$F$-regularity and compute the quasi-$F$-split threshold of the cone over the ordinary cusp.

papers.title: When is the canonical conductor minimal?
papers.abstract: For a one dimensional analytically unramified Cohen-Macaulay local ring $R$, the blowup algebra of the canonical ideal is a module finite birational extension. The conductor of this extension always contains the conductor of $R$. We study the case when there is equality. This is the case where $R$ is far from being almost Gorenstein. We characterise such rings among Arf domains and numerical semigroup rings. As an application, we compute the cohomology annihilator ideal of an explicit family of rings and show it to be equal to the conductor ideal.

papers.title: Hankel and Multiplication Tensor Completions for Cactus Rank
papers.abstract: We show that the Hankel flat extension formulation of the cactus algorithm is equivalent to a completion problem for multiplication tensors of Artinian Gorenstein algebras. The unknown Hankel moments are canonically identified with the undetermined tensor coefficients, and under this identification the symbolic multiplication matrices and their commutation equations coincide. This shows that the usual degree extension formulation is a coordinate realization of a variable extension problem with marked generators. We further use Borel-fixed and squat staircases to reduce the family of candidate basis shapes in the resulting algorithm.

papers.title: Filtrations on D-modules and multiplicities of roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we relate multiplicities of Bernstein--Sato-type polynomials with respect to a function f to several singularity invariants. First, we introduce certain ``mod'' b-functions and show that they characterize the weight filtration on the localization of a simple algebraic holonomic D-module along f, and we provide an algorithm to compute them. Second, we show that they can be approximated by the multiplicities of roots of power b-functions (i.e., the b-functions with respect to powers of f). Furthermore, we give a sharp upper bound for the Hodge level of elements given by a certain sum of such multiplicities. Next, we give an effective asymptotic solution to the Gelfand problem by determining an explicit threshold after which every integer shift of a root of b_f(s) is a pole of the Archimedean zeta function of f. We also show that the order of these poles is equal to the nilpotency index of the logarithmic monodromy operator, which we further express as the limit of the multiplicities of roots of power b-functions. We define several filtrations, relating them to the weight and Hodge filtrations, based upon which we leave some open questions that we address in the affirmative in the case when f has a homogeneous isolated singularity, or it is a hyperplane arrangement, or a semi-invariant on a spherical variety. We give several immediate applications to our results, including a solution to a question of Torrelli on whether 1/f lies in the intersection complex of the hypersurface of f if and only if -1 is a simple root of b_f(s).

papers.title: Big Finitistic Dimensions of Formal Power Series Rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we completely investigate what the big finitistic projective dimension (resp., big finitistic flat dimension) pair, which abbreviates FPD pair (resp., FFD pair), of a commutative ring and of its formal power series ring can be. When the ring is Noetherian, both invariants increase by one. In general, for every \(n\ge0\) and every \(d\) with \(n+1\le d\le\infty\), the FFD pair \((n,d)\) can be realized; the FPD pairs \((n,d)\) can be realized when \(n\ge1\), also for \((0,1)\) and \((0,\infty)\). However, the FPD pair \((0,2)\) is impossible. For perfect coefficients, we prove that the existence of a commutative perfect ring \(R\) with \(\FPD(R[[x]])=3\) is equivalent to the continuum hypothesis. Under the continuum hypothesis, every finite integer \(n\ge2\) admits a commutative local perfect ring \(R\) with \(\FFD(R[[x]])=1\) and \(\FPD(R[[x]])=n+2\). And for each such \(n\), the existence of a perfect coefficient ring with projective value \(n+2\) does not imply the continuum hypothesis.

papers.title: Lefschetz Properties of complete intersesctions and maximal variation of hyperplane sections
papers.abstract: For an artinian complete intersection of forms of degree $d$, we prove that the multiplication by a general linear form is injective up to degree $\frac{3d-1}2$, independently of the number of variables. This is accomplished using algebraic and geometric properties of the union of two complete intersection curves and their general hyperplane sections. As a consequence, we solve, for any $d\ge 4$, the problem about the maximal variation of the hyperplane sections of a smooth hypersurface of degree $d$ posed by A. Beauville.

papers.title: Ideals of 2-minors of nearly determinantal matrices
papers.abstract: Motivated by the study of prime binomial ideals with Cohen--Macaulay quotients and linear resolutions, we introduce nearly determinantal matrices, a class of matrices obtained by repeating variables from the preceding rows in the last row. We characterize the primality of their ideals of $2$-minors in terms of an associated directed graph with row labels. For every prime case, we prove that the quotient is a normal Cohen--Macaulay domain and determine its graded Betti numbers. Finally, a prime ideal in this family has a linear resolution if and only if the matrix has three rows or two columns.

papers.title: Finiteness of local cohomology modules over arbitrary regular local rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider arbitrary regular local ring $S$ and an ideal $J\subset S$ whose minimal primes are cohomologically complete intersection. In Section 2, using the Mayer-Vietoris spectral sequence, we construct examples of local cohomology modules $H^i_J (S)$, whose set of associated primes is finite, where minimal primes satisfy the `Dropping Condition'. As a special case, we show that when minimal primes of $J$ are part of a specific regular system of parameters satisfy the `Dropping Condition', the set of associated primes of $H^i_J (S)$ is finite. In Section 3, we prove the main result without the `Dropping Condition' and as a special case, we show that when minimal primes of $J$ are part of a specific regular system of parameters, the set of associated primes of $H^i_J (S)$ is finite. These examples of local cohomology modules include the cases whose associated primes can contain prime number $p$, but still the set is finite.
